root_cause: The control plane has strict parsers for individual Project, Skill, Workflow, and Composition declarations, but no package-level manifest or verifier owns cross-file identity, default entrypoint, capability/provider coverage, and installation integrity. Domain examples therefore remain prose or isolated fixtures instead of one reusable customer-agent starter.
causal_chain: Authoring validates one declaration at a time.
Composition validates one base Workflow plus explicitly supplied Skill contracts.
No manifest enumerates the declarations that belong to one supported starter.
No verifier proves unique Skill/Workflow identities, valid overlays, default entrypoints, or Provider coverage across the package.
No CLI can safely copy a verified package into a target workspace.
Users must reconstruct examples manually and can create inconsistent or non-runnable combinations.
rejected_hypotheses: Documentation snippets are sufficient; they do not prove cross-file compilation or Provider coverage.
The starter should modify customer application source; a development Harness package must remain separate from the produced application runtime.
A new customer-agent runtime is necessary; existing WorkflowSpec, Composer, Dispatcher, and Provider contracts already own execution semantics.
